subject: Diffusion rate's relationship with different movement models

messages.author: 0cade8d1de19e864
messages.subject: Diffusion rate's relationship with different movement models
parts:
Hi all, 

Hopefully this is an easy one and I'm misunderstanding something. I have a question about diffusion rates produced in ctmm. 

For context, I have a dataset comprised of 52 individuals GPS tracked before, during and after fire and I'm interested in seeing if fire led to an increase or decrease in diffusion rates. Fortunately, the species I'm working with had very fast range crossing times, so stationarity is easy to confirm and diffusion effective sample sizes are relatively large (often between 50 - 150) for each individual and time period. 

I've used ctmm.select to fit movement models and whilst OUF or OUf was often selected, OU models were also supported in a reasonable number of individuals. The question I have is this: How much of a difference in diffusion rate estimates would I expect to see if these estimates were predicted from different movement models? Is it crucial to ensure any comparison of diffusion rates occurs only within predictions from the same movement model (OUF, OUf, OU etc)?

I'll have a play around with visualising estimates from each movement model type out of curiosity, but if you have any simple theoretical/practical guidance to give here, that would be very much appreciated!

Thanks, 

Mark

messages.author: 40fd627580dd34f5
messages.subject: Re: Diffusion rate's relationship with different movement models
parts:
Hi Mark,

The diffusion rates are maximized across time-lag to be comparable across models. There is an upcoming paper describing this.

Best,
Chris
